questions.question: When students board a school bus, the driver should:

options.text: Read a book.
Check all mirrors.
Only look at the students.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check all mirrors.
questions.explanation: While students board, watch all mirrors. Look for students who may be running to catch the bus.

questions.question: At stops, a driver should:

options.text: Leave the bus.
Warn exiting passengers about potential hazards.
Talk with other bus drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn exiting passengers about potential hazards.
questions.explanation: Warn passengers about dangers. Tell them to watch their step when exiting on the lowered stairways.

questions.question: When approaching a drawbridge with a green light:

options.text: You must stop.
You may proceed without stopping.
You must wait for the light to change to yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may proceed without stopping.
questions.explanation: A bus does not need to stop at a drawbridge with a green light. However, slow down and check that it is safe to cross.

questions.question: When students are being picked up by a school bus:

options.text: The students should wait at a designated bus stop.
The driver should pick up students whether or not they are at the designated bus stop.
The parents should choose where the bus stop will be located.

questions.correctAnswerText: The students should wait at a designated bus stop.
questions.explanation: Load and unload students only at designated stops. These stops must be approved by school district officials.

questions.question: If a bus leans toward the outside of a banked curve, the bus is:

options.text: Moving too slowly.
Moving at the proper speed.
Moving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Moving too fast.
questions.explanation: Reduce speed when entering a curve. If the bus leans toward the outside, you are going too fast.

questions.question: At a passive railroad crossing, the decision to proceed:

options.text: Rests with the driver.
Is indicated by a control device.
Is decided by the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rests with the driver.
questions.explanation: A passive crossing has no traffic control device. The driver decides whether it is safe to cross the tracks.

questions.question: When making a stop to pick up students, a driver should ensure all surrounding traffic has stopped before:

options.text: Opening the door and signaling for the students to approach.
Turning on the alternating red lights.
Pulling over to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening the door and signaling for the students to approach.
questions.explanation: Make sure all traffic around you has stopped before opening the door and calling students to the bus.

questions.question: When approaching a school bus stop, the driver should:

options.text: Honk the horn.
Drive slowly.
Talk to students on the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly.
questions.explanation: Always approach bus stops slowly and with care.

questions.question: Before a bus enters a curve, the driver should:

options.text: Increase their speed.
Not change their speed.
Reduce their speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce their speed.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. Be extra careful on wet or slippery roads.

questions.question: The standee line:

options.text: Is a line that passengers should not cross.
Is a line upon which passengers should stand.
Is a line that should be used as passengers exit the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a line that passengers should not cross.
questions.explanation: Passengers cannot stand in front of the back of the driver's seat. A standee line marks this boundary on the floor.

questions.question: What should you do with roof hatches on buses?

options.text: Remove them before driving.
Keep them closed while driving.
Lock them in a partially-open position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lock them in a partially-open position.
questions.explanation: You can lock some roof hatches partially open for fresh air. Do not make this a regular practice. Opening hatches will slightly increase the bus's height.

questions.question: Where should students wait when a school bus picks them up?

options.text: At a designated bus stop.
The driver will pick them up anywhere on their way to the stop.
Parents choose where the bus stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a designated bus stop.
questions.explanation: School bus drivers can only pick up students at official stops. These stops are chosen by school officials.

questions.question: What does ABS help you do?

options.text: Drive faster.
Drive less carefully.
Keep control on slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep control on slippery roads.
questions.explanation: ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System) stops your wheels from locking up on slippery surfaces. This helps you maintain control when you brake hard. Drive a bus with ABS the same way as a bus without ABS.

questions.question: What should you check when inspecting the inside of a bus?

options.text: Lock every emergency exit window.
Check that every railing is secure.
Remove loose handholds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that every railing is secure.
questions.explanation: Check that all handholds and railings are secure and safe to use. Make sure everything inside the bus is in good working condition.

questions.question: Where are the danger zones around a school bus?

options.text: Only in front of the bus.
Only at the rear and left side.
All around the bus — front, sides, and rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: All around the bus — front, sides, and rear.
questions.explanation: Danger zones are areas where children can be hit by the bus or another vehicle. These zones are in front, on both sides, and at the rear of the bus. They extend 10 feet from every side of the bus.

questions.question: How should students safely exit a school bus?

options.text: Stay seated until the driver tells them to leave.
Stand up and move to the door while the bus is slowing down.
Exit and stand right next to the bus while it drives away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay seated until the driver tells them to leave.
questions.explanation: Students must stay in their seats until the driver tells them it is safe to exit. After leaving, they should walk at least 10 feet away so the driver can see them clearly.

questions.question: What should you do about backing up a school bus?

options.text: Do it whenever you need to turn around.
Avoid it whenever possible.
Only do it in the morning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid it whenever possible.
questions.explanation: Avoid backing up a school bus. Only back up if there is no safe alternative. Follow all safety rules if you must drive in reverse.

questions.question: What should the driver watch for as students exit the bus?

options.text: That they leave in pairs.
That clothing or bodies do not get caught on railings or doors.
That they do not talk while exiting.

questions.correctAnswerText: That clothing or bodies do not get caught on railings or doors.
questions.explanation: Students can be injured or killed if their clothing, accessories, or bodies get caught on a railing or door. The driver must watch carefully as all students exit to make sure they reach a safe location.

questions.question: What do crossover mirrors help the driver see?

options.text: The danger zones in front of the bus.
The rear bumper.
The left side of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The danger zones in front of the bus.
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors show the driver the danger zone in front of the bus. They also show danger zones on the left and right sides, from the front bumper to the service door.

questions.question: What should you do when you reach railroad tracks while driving a school bus?

options.text: Look at the tracks and continue without stopping.
Stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest rail.
Stop 75 feet before the nearest rail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest rail.
questions.explanation: Stop before all railroad crossings. Stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail. This gives you the best view. Look and listen for trains before crossing.
